questions.q: Deficiency of which vitamin causes scurvy?
questions.e: Scurvy, marked by bleeding gums, results from lack of Vitamin C (ascorbic acid).

questions.q: The largest organ of the human body is the
questions.e: The skin is the largest organ by surface area and weight. The liver is the largest internal organ and gland.

questions.q: During photosynthesis, green plants absorb ______ from the air.
questions.e: Plants take in carbon dioxide and, with water and sunlight, make glucose and release oxygen.

questions.q: The SI unit of electric charge is the
questions.e: Electric charge is measured in coulomb. Ampere is the unit of current, volt of potential difference and ohm of resistance.

questions.q: The chemical name of baking soda is
questions.e: Baking soda is sodium hydrogencarbonate, NaHCO₃. Washing soda is sodium carbonate.

questions.q: The wing mirror fitted on the side of a vehicle to see traffic behind is a
questions.e: A convex mirror always forms a smaller, erect image and gives a wide field of view, so it suits a wing mirror.

questions.q: India's first satellite, launched in 1975, was
questions.e: Aryabhata was launched on 19 April 1975 with a Soviet rocket. Bhaskara followed in 1979.

questions.q: A sphygmomanometer is used to measure
questions.e: A sphygmomanometer measures blood pressure. A clinical thermometer measures body temperature.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Mars Orbiter Mission (Mangalyaan)
I. It entered the orbit of Mars in September 2014.
II. India succeeded in reaching Mars orbit on its very first attempt.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: Mangalyaan entered Mars orbit on 24 September 2014, making India the first country to do so on its first attempt.

questions.q: Which vitamin contains the metal cobalt?
questions.e: Vitamin B12 (cobalamin) contains cobalt. Its deficiency leads to pernicious anaemia.

questions.q: The Indian Institute of Science, Bengaluru, was set up in 1909 mainly through the initiative of
questions.e: Jamsetji Tata proposed and funded the Indian Institute of Science, with support from the Mysore state.

questions.q: Plaster of Paris is chemically
questions.e: Plaster of Paris is CaSO₄·½H₂O, made by heating gypsum (CaSO₄·2H₂O) to about 373 K.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about sound
I. It travels faster in water than in air.
II. It can travel through a vacuum.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: Sound is a mechanical wave needing a medium, and it moves faster in liquids than in gases. It cannot pass through vacuum.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the blue colour of the sky
I. It is caused by scattering of sunlight by air molecules.
II. Red light is scattered more than blue light.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: Rayleigh scattering is stronger for shorter wavelengths, so blue is scattered more than red. Statement II is therefore wrong.

questions.q: A fuse wire used in electrical circuits is made of a material with
o: high melting point and low resistance
high melting point and high resistance
very high conductivity and high melting point
questions.e: A fuse is made of a tin–lead alloy with a low melting point, so it melts and breaks the circuit when excess current flows.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India's Moon missions
I. The Vikram lander of Chandrayaan-2 made a successful soft landing in 2019.
II. India became the fourth country to soft-land on the Moon with Chandrayaan-3 in 2023.
Which of the above is/are correct?
questions.e: Chandrayaan-2's lander crashed near the surface in September 2019. Chandrayaan-3 landed on 23 August 2023, after the USSR, USA and China.

questions.q: A 12 V battery is connected to a 4 Ω resistor in series with a parallel combination of 6 Ω and 3 Ω resistors. The current drawn from the battery is
questions.e: 6 Ω and 3 Ω in parallel give 2 Ω. Total resistance = 4 + 2 = 6 Ω, so I = 12 ÷ 6 = 2 A.

questions.q: What volume of 0.2 M NaOH solution is needed to neutralise exactly 20 mL of 0.1 M H₂SO₄?
questions.e: H₂SO₄ gives 2 H⁺ per molecule: 20 × 0.1 × 2 = 4 mmol H⁺. NaOH volume = 4 ÷ 0.2 = 20 mL.

questions.q: A concave lens has a focal length of 25 cm. Its power is
questions.e: Power = 1/f in metres = 1/(−0.25) = −4 dioptre. A concave lens has a negative focal length.

questions.q: Which of the following CSIR laboratory–city pairs is NOT correctly matched?
questions.e: The National Geophysical Research Institute (NGRI) is in Hyderabad. CFTRI is at Mysuru, NCL at Pune and CECRI at Karaikudi.
